In parseRefreshTokenResponse, when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, it safeParses with minimumTokenResponseSchema (only access_token + expiry) instead of salesforceTokenSchema, and z.object's default stripping drops instance_url, signature, etc. from the persisted key. So enabling the credential-sharing feature (unrelated to Salesforce's own flow) corrupts Salesforce credentials on next refresh. All elements of the mechanism are visible in the diff.

judged_text: When credential sharing is enabled, parseRefreshTokenResponse applies minimumTokenResponseSchema to Salesforce's response (Salesforce never uses the sync endpoint itself), and z.object's default key-stripping reduces accessTokenParsed.data to {access_token}, so the persisted key loses instance_url, id, signature, scope and token_type. Enabling credential sharing for other apps corrupts every Salesforce credential on its next refresh: the stored key no longer carries instance_url, so the next jsforce.Connection hits the default login domain and API calls fail for customers on My Domain instances.

adjudication.rationale: In `parseRefreshTokenResponse` the choice of schema is gated only on `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`, not on the app being refreshed. Salesforce refresh (`packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`) calls `parseRefreshTokenResponse(accessTokenJson, salesforceTokenSchema)`, so if credential sharing is enabled for any reason and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is set, it will validate with `minimumTokenResponseSchema` instead of `salesforceTokenSchema`. Since `z.object(...)` strips unknown keys by default, the parsed `accessTokenParsed.data` will drop Salesforce fields like `instance_url`, `id`, `signature`, `scope`, `token_type`, and the code then persists `{ ...accessTokenParsed.data, refresh_token: ... }`, overwriting the credential key without those fields. This is a verifiable data-loss/breakage path introduced by the diff.
